description_paragraphs: (Arthur Rankin, 1982, United Kingdom, 93 min, in English)

The Last Unicorn is a fantasy film about the last remaining unicorn on earth who leaves her home in the lilac woods in the hope that she will find another unicorn somewhere in the world. A wondrous adventure begins; capture, exhibition, confrontation with the evil Red Bull, friendship with an inept magician and the release of other unicorns from a horrible fate in the sea. Finally, the unicorns return to the lilac woods to live happily ever after.
Synopsis courtesy of Park Circus
(Biff Hartwell, 2026, United States, 65 min, in English)
A doomed transgender creature becomes psychically entangled with a medieval nun in this Super 8 rock opera.
Synopsis courtesy of Biff Hartwell
SCREENS WITH THE SOUL SNATCHER
(Biff Hartwell & Mitchell Pollitt, 2024, United States, 15 min, in English)
After unearthing the skeleton of a priest, a group of debaucherous youngsters are punished for their sins.
(Avalon Fast, 2025, Canada, 111 min, in English)

Emily is the root cause of two devastating tragedies very early in her life. She feels the weight of these accidents like a curse has been placed upon her. Her dad suggests she go to a Camp for troubled youth to ease her guilt; she can be a counsellor there. When Emily arrives, she is taken in by the other counselors, they accept her as she is and wrap her in a veil of peace & forgiveness. Emily stands at the forefront of a new kind of life, but there’s a voice out there in the woods she can’t quite seem to ignore. The voice is whispering, she’s telling Emily to go home.
Synopsis courtesy of Dark Sky Films
(Lucio Castro, 2025, United States & Argentina, 81 min, in English and Spanish with English subtitles)

Adnan, a young art student, arrives in New York City to flat-sit for the summer. He begins interning at a gallery where an unconventional older artist he once encountered is being exhibited. As moments from his past and present begin to intertwine, a series of encounters – both artistic and erotic – open cracks in his everyday reality.
Synopsis courtesy of Strand Releasing
(Rose Glass, 2024, United States, 104 min, in English)

From Director Rose Glass comes an electric new love story; reclusive gym manager Lou falls hard for Jackie, an ambitious bodybuilder headed through town to Vegas in pursuit of her dream. But their love ignites violence, pulling them deep into the web of Lou’s criminal family.
Synopsis courtesy of A24

description_paragraphs: Sci-Fi heads unite! Cyber strikes, future tech, and stargazing adventurers dominate this month’s LOCALS ONLY event. This sci-fi themed block is sure to fling you across time and scramble your understanding of what it means to be human:
THE LAST FLIGHT by Daniel Mogg: Amid a global cyber strike that leads to a permanent ban on air travel, an isolated fugitive family races to catch the last private flight to freedom. (5 min)

AXIOM by Katy Joy & Blake Rizzo: An android travels back into the past to retrieve a mysterious software from a CEO’s home, only to quickly uncover hidden truths about the mission’s objective. (7 min)
STARDATE: UNKNOWN by Andrew Davies: The crew of the UCS Reliant must survive alone on an alien planet when the technology they rely on fails them. (4 min)
STARGAZER by Justin Robert Vinall: A fragmented astronomer looks to the stars to find comfort in the darkest of places. (15 min)
This event is presented in partnership with the Northwest Film Forum. Join us for a screening and Q&A with drinks to follow at Linda’s Tavern!
Thursday July 30th at the Northwest Film Forum. Doors at 6:30, Films at 7. See ya at the movies!

description_paragraphs: (Adam Sekuler, 2024, United States, 78 min, in English)

The Flamingo is a feature-length documentary that intimately follows Mary Phillips, a 63- year-old divorcee who reinvents herself after 13 years of celibacy and isolation. Set against the backdrop of dungeon parties, road trips, and moments of deep reflection, the film traces Mary’s journey as she claims her power through sexual play and healing touch within the BDSM community. It is a coming-out tale—both sexually and emotionally—as Mary navigates the complexities of desire, aging, and connection.

The film offers an unflinching look at how Mary redefines herself, whether by providing advice over pink lemonade to a neighbor curious about the swingers community, leading platonic cuddling sessions, or recounting her experiences with young women around a bonfire. Mary’s role as a healer—both physical and emotional—comes through as she mothers those around her, even as she grapples with the challenges of her own life, including a strained relationship with her daughter.
Through its observational and poetic style, The Flamingo explores the interplay between Mary’s joie de vivre and her existential questions about what life holds as she enters her final years.

Ultimately, The Flamingo offers a fresh perspective on aging and female sexuality, challenging viewers to see aging not as a process of decline but as a time to reclaim pleasure, self-expression, and autonomy.

description_paragraphs: (Ross McElwee, United States, 1985, 158 min, in English)

Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the lingering aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman’s 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South. A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, SHERMAN’S MARCH sketches its characters with novelistic sensitivity: Pat, an aspiring actress with a yen for Burt Reynolds; Claudia, a roller-skating interior designer; Jackie, the activist whose anti-nuclear advocacy dovetails with Ross’s deepest fears; and above all, Charleen Swansea, Ross’s mentor and a one-woman Greek chorus of unsolicited romantic counsel. A landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV, SHERMAN’S MARCH is now available in a new 4K restoration.
Synopsis courtesy of Music Box Films
